business.title: Context-dependent vascular effects of platycodin D: inhibition of neointima formation but aggravation of atherosclerosis with involvement of mTORC1 signaling
business.description: Platycodin D (PD), a triterpenoid saponin from Platycodon grandiflorus, has been reported to have cardiovascular activity, but its actions in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and atherosclerosis remain unclear. We integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation, VSMC assays, and two mouse carotid models. In VSMCs cultured under basal conditions, PD reduced viability and BrdU incorporation, downregulated cyclin D1/E1, and induced TUNEL positivity and cleaved caspase-3. At the cellular level, PD activated mTORC1-associated signaling, increased p70S6K and eIF2α phosphorylation, increased ATF4 protein and activated ATF6, impaired autophagic flux, and induced CHOP-associated endoplasmic reticulum stress. Rapamycin and 4-phenylbutyric acid attenuated PD-induced apoptosis, whereas MHY1485 and thapsigargin exacerbated it. Perivascular PD reduced neointimal hyperplasia after complete carotid ligation in C57BL/6J mice. In contrast, PD accelerated early carotid atherosclerosis after partial ligation in ApoE–/– mice fed a high-fat diet. Under ox-LDL challenge, PD increased VSMC lipid accumulation, Olr1/Cd36 expression, mTORC1-p70S6K signaling, and BrdU incorporation; rapamycin limited these effects. These findings suggest that PD activates an mTORC1-associated stress program whose vascular outcome depends on lipid and flow context. PD may have local anti-neointimal potential but warrants caution in hyperlipidemic atherosclerosis.

business.title: Integrated intelligent smoke management system: integrating electrostatic precipitation with PID-controlled air recirculation for charcoal-grill restaurant kitchens
business.description: Charcoal-grill restaurants can contribute to localized air pollution through emissions of particulate matter, including PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀, particularly in small kitchens with limited ventilation. This study developed and experimentally evaluated an intelligent smoke management system integrating a dual-stage electrostatic precipitator (ESP), PID-controlled multi-pass air recirculation, and a compact smoke-capture hood for small charcoal-grill restaurants. The prototype was tested in an enclosed kitchen with a volume of 25 m3 under Single-pass and Recirculation operating modes at airflow velocities of 2 and 3 m/s using six paired experimental runs (n = 6). System performance was evaluated based on PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ removal efficiency, particulate removal rate, Equivalent Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADRₑq), and electrical energy consumption. The results showed that the Recirculation mode at an airflow velocity of 3 m/s achieved the highest particulate-removal efficiencies, reaching 95.15% for PM₂.₅ and 95.50% for PM₁₀. These values were significantly higher than those obtained under the corresponding Single-pass condition (p < 0.001). Under this operating condition, the measured average system-level electrical power was 68.2 W, corresponding to an energy consumption of 11.4 Wh per 10-min experimental cycle. The equivalent Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADRₑq), estimated from the experimentally derived airflow and measured particulate-removal efficiency, was approximately 813.1 m3/h for PM₂.₅ and 816.1 m3/h for PM₁₀. These findings demonstrate that integrating a dual-stage ESP with PID-controlled multi-pass air recirculation improved particulate-removal performance under the specific experimental conditions investigated. However, because the system was evaluated at a single test site using six matched experimental runs, further validation across different kitchen environments and cooking loads, together with direct ozone and VOC measurements and long-term operational assessment, is required before broader commercial applicability can be established.
